title: What the Channel Feeds
logline: In a village fed by one shared reservoir, farmers wait for the gate to open, and a single release of water starts a chain that ends, months later, at a bowl of rice on a table none of them will ever see.

object.note: Object 9 (identity not chosen) could enter only if something that exists because of the whole chain, such as hand-milled rice or a winnowing basket, is genuinely given. Never staged.

thread_in.thread: If nothing passes across and yet everything continues, something must connect it all: from nets passed hand to hand to a tank gate opening, the first link in a chain that ends in a bowl of rice.

thread_out.thread: The water that starts the chain meets a machine that stopped: a repairer opening a water pump to find not one cause but several small ones.

requirements: A working tank-fed irrigation system with a visible water-sharing arrangement
A family plot that can be followed through most of one season
Willingness to show disputes or hardship honestly, not only a good outcome

suggestions.name: A minor-tank paddy village in the Rajarata dry zone
suggestions.why: Small, tank-fed paddy systems with rotational water sharing are widespread and long-established across this region.
suggestions.season_notes: Yala or Maha cultivation season, depending on the tank
suggestions.verify: A specific tank, family and water-sharing arrangement must be identified and confirmed.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed.

lesson.in_simple_terms: One meal needs many different supports at once. A seed starts the rice plant, but water and fertiliser keep it growing for months, and each helps in its own way.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: එක් වේලක බතක් හට ගන්නට බීජය, වතුර, පොහොර, අත් ගණනාවක් හා කාලගුණය වැනි බොහෝ ප්‍රත්‍යයන් එකවර උදව් විය යුතු අතර, ඒ එකිනෙක උදව් වන්නේ තමන්ගේම ආකාරයෙනි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma calls a cause that especially keeps a life going 'nutriment' (āhāra). Margaya's own image is a rice seedling: the seed's strength is chief for the plant to begin, but fertiliser and water are chief for it to grow and last for months. The texts also teach that nothing conditioned arises from a single condition, and that different conditions help in different ways, like the match-head and the matchbox that together make a flame. Cause and effect can be told briefly or in full detail, and both accounts are part of complete understanding.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The farmers' meeting, the gate opening and the water reaching the last field in the rotation show supports that no one family controls. Over months the crop's colour changes with water and weather, until a first meal of the new rice is eaten, and the viewer can set the family's short answer ('the rain came') against the long chain the film has just followed.

key_terms.en: condition; what helps something arise, persist or grow
condition-power; the specific way one thing helps another

lesson.caution: This is not a warm 'everything is connected' slogan or a wellness message about feeding yourself well: the texts name specific, bounded kinds of support, and they call these nutriments because they keep the round of rebirth going.
lesson.builds_on: Group 8 ended with the last moments of one life conditioning the next, with nothing passing across, and asked what connects it all; this film answers with conditions you can watch: water, seed, labour and weather each holding up one harvest.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
